title: Graphic Storytelling — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Graphic Storytelling's rich face: a strip whose layout your hands time, blind, against McCloud's time-is-space, and the two Daily Page roughs that put the color claims to a viewer, laid beside the sections they test, with the fingerprint of the words each was made against so the page can say when a piece may lag the text. I grow when the entry is enriched again, and I expect to be re-tuned when the page's revision lands; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: "Time is rendered as space" is McCloud's own (secondary sources quote "time and space are one and the same", about p. 100). "Simply lasts longer" and the gutter half are the page's own strengthening, attributed to him. Secondary sources give his hedges: a panel's durations are "defined more by the contents of the panel than by the panel itself", and differences of shape "can affect the reading experience". No source was found for a wider gutter lasting longer. Checked against secondary sources only, not the book (about pp. 99–101). A possible sentence: "time is drawn as space: a wider panel can feel longer, though McCloud says a panel's contents set its time more than its shape", with the gutter clause given to the craft or held until it is found. The revision draft repeats the sentence ("A wider panel, or more gutter, simply lasts longer"), so this applies when it lands. The time-is-space piece times the two halves apart; no reader has run it yet, so there are no numbers.

offers.section: The live edge — black-and-white, plus one bold color
offers.what: "Restraint as the source of the punch": the gathered color hold (2026-10-28, one viewer, scored out of 5) completes the bullet rather than contradicting it. Red from the moment the glove falls (panel 3 of 6) and held scored 3, below all ink at 4; red withheld and revealed on the close-up's downbeat scored 5; full palette 2. The bullet's own "because" ("the page taught the reader that color is rare") describes the take that scored 5. Restraint was necessary, not sufficient; the reveal on the beat did the rest. A clause naming the reveal would say so. The scroll's study entry says the held take is red "from the first panel"; the rough's key (line 91) makes it panel 3, a bundle fix. The baton and the revision draft already carry the finding.
The comment "CLAUDE → LOUDON: hero + icon pending" under the title is stale: the hero and icon exist in the bundle. The revision draft drops it.

The revision the baton lands renames both headings this face is keyed to and removes all three anchor phrases, so every piece will drop into Lost its place. The baton's next move should gain a line: re-key the rich manifest's two sections (time is space beside "The frame and the gutter" under "The tools, each an expectation to bend"; the two roughs under "Shown, not argued"), re-anchor the three pieces, and re-stamp. Approval of these sections should wait until that is done.

verdicts.why: A real test with a working size control, and it walks up, but its verdict lines overclaim one run: with a true equal 1.3× effect at 25% scatter it says "your holds split them" in 33% of runs and "time was not drawn as space" in 51%. Split only when h(wide)/h(gutter) clears ×1.1 in all three stories (≤1/8 by chance), soften the failure line, state that either half showing longer has a ≤1/4 chance, and add the equal-effect check to check.mjs.

pieces.by: the Maker · SVG ink strips, timed by hand
pieces.title: Does a wider panel last longer?
pieces.caption: **The page's line, after McCloud, put to your hands.** It walks up from two panels and the gap you fill (closure), through a strip whose layout you drag while its drawing stays still, to a stopwatch you hold. Then fifteen strips: three small stories, each in five layouts, shuffled, each at a slightly different size. For each one you hold for as long as the wait felt, and the layouts are compared only after the last hold. The wide panel and the wide gutter each add the same length along the reading line. A tall panel adds the same panel area across it, the control that tells space along the line from plain size. It can come out against the page, and it can split the sentence's two halves, panel and gutter. One reader, fifteen holds: a reading, not a law.

sections.heading: The live edge — black-and-white, plus one bold color

verdicts.why: A blind test of the restraint claim, and its scores match the scroll (5/4/4/3/2). One caption fix: the held take is red from the moment the glove falls (panel 3, per its key at line 91), not from the first panel.
Tests the color script with color as the only variable (the arcs could have lost to the moods), the caption matches the scroll record, and it warns honestly that answers are lost on reload.

pieces.title: The color hold · Daily Page rough, 2026-10-28
pieces.caption: **The color hold, as it was played.** Five blind takes of one six-panel ink strip on an 84 bpm clock, differing only in where one red sits and on which beat it arrives; the key shows after you rate. Loudon's scores, one viewer, one sitting, out of 5: red withheld and revealed on the close-up's downbeat 5; all ink 4; red two beats late 4; red from the moment the glove falls (panel 3 of 6) and held 3; full palette 2. The full palette lost, as the next paragraph says, but restraint alone didn't win: the same red, shown from the glove's fall on, scored below no color at all. What hit hardest was the color withheld, then revealed on the beat. It plays a kick on the clock after a click; no agent has heard it.

pieces.title: One strip, six stories · Daily Page rough, 2026-10-29
pieces.caption: **A color script you can play.** The same six frames, drawing and clock, with color the only variable. Four takes hold one palette throughout (anger, nostalgia, wistfulness, depression). Two move it across the panels, warming toward the end or draining toward it: a color script in six frames. In Loudon's sit the two arcs carried far more than the moods, and the draining one was the clearest story and "by far" the most emotional. The warming one failed because the drawing contradicted it: a tool can't carry a meaning the other tools contradict. One viewer, one sitting. Its answers live in the frame and are lost on a reload, so copy them out before you leave. It plays sound after a click; no agent has heard it.
